description:
FILED s510 (Fable, 2026-10-06) from the perf round 40 review probes (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s510/review/p40/u.pl and b1.pl .. b5.pl); main 9364ae68, perl 5.40.3.

  sub w { my ($h) = @_; binmode($h, ":utf8"); print $h "caf\x{e9}\n"; }
  open(my $fh, ">", $T) or die;  w($fh);  close($fh);  print -s $T;        perl: 6      PCL: 0   (the 6 bytes arrive only when the PROCESS exits)
  my $copy = $fh; binmode($copy, ":utf8"); print $copy "caf\x{e9}\n"; print $fh "tail\n"; close($fh);
                                                                          perl: 11 bytes   PCL: 6 at exit -- "tail\n" is LOST
  RIGHT today: `binmode($_[0], ":utf8")` (the alias), plain `binmode($h)` on a byte handle (no rebuild), binmode in the scope that opened the handle, `open(..., ">:utf8", ...)`.

CAUSE (read, cl/pcl-runtime.lisp %p-binmode-impl -> %p-rebuild-fd-stream): SBCL cannot change an fd-stream\x27s external format, so a binmode that CHANGES the discipline dups the descriptor, builds a new fd-stream, CLOSES the original and installs the new one in the ONE variable it was given (`%p-install-fh fh new`).  A lexical handle is the stream object in the variable\x27s box, so every other copy of the handle still holds the closed original.  The function\x27s own comment already names this failure for the no-change case (fixed there by the EQUAL test); the real-change case is the same hole.  Perl\x27s handle is ONE IO object behind every copy.

WHY IT MATTERS: "a helper that sets the encoding on the handle it is given" is ordinary code (`sub setup { my ($fh) = @_; binmode($fh, ":encoding(UTF-8)") }`), and after it every print by the caller goes nowhere, silently.

DIRECTIONS (not designed; each needs a measurement on the print / readline rows -- perf round 40 found %p-resolve-fh at 13.7 % of a print already):
  (a) ONE identity per handle: the open creates a wrapper with a swappable target (what the STANDARD handles already have: %p-std-rebuild swaps the stream under every copy of STDOUT), and the rebuild swaps the target instead of the variable\x27s value;
  (b) never rebuild: keep the fd-stream in the byte discipline and move the layer into PCL\x27s own read / write path, with the layer state keyed on the stream object (as $. and $| are);
  (c) the cheap half-fix, if (a)/(b) are too big for one batch: the rebuild does NOT close the original but turns it into a forwarder -- only possible if the original can be made to forward, which a plain fd-stream cannot; so probably not available.  Say why if it is rejected.
Probe table to take against perl before designing: every way a handle gets a second name (assignment, sub argument copy, `\*FH` and `*FH{IO}`, a hash / array element, a closure capture, `local *FH = $fh`, `open(my $dup, ">&", $fh)` -- a REAL second descriptor in perl, must stay separate), crossed with binmode to and from :raw / :utf8 / :encoding(UTF-8) / :crlf, on output and on a partly-read input handle.

=== s510 (Fable, 2026-10-06 late): THE DESIGN -- the primitive was TESTED and the fix is SMALL: change the stream's encoding IN PLACE, keep the stream object ===
None of directions (a)/(b)/(c) above is needed.  The comment in %p-rebuild-fd-stream ("SBCL has no (setf stream-external-format)") is true for the PUBLIC interface (checked on SBCL 2.6.0: the setf function is undefined), but the routine make-fd-stream itself uses to install an external format can be called again on a LIVE stream:
    (let* ((entry (sb-impl::get-external-format-or-lose ef))
           (canon (sb-impl::canonize-external-format ef entry))
           (pos   (and in (ignore-errors (file-position s)))))
      (when out (finish-output s))
      (sb-impl::set-fd-stream-routines s (quote character) canon entry in out NIL nil)   ; buffer-p NIL: keep the buffers
      (when pos (ignore-errors (file-position s pos))))                                     ; re-seek: discards read-ahead decoded the old way
MEASURED on SBCL 2.6.0 (the version CI and the install matrix pin), probes in ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s510/review/binmode/*.lisp:
  - OUTPUT, switching latin-1 -> utf-8 -> latin-1 between writes: the SAME object (eq), bytes 61 E2 98 BA 62 E9 3F exactly as expected;
  - the #2777 shape (two variables, one stream; switch through one, write through both, close the other): 11 bytes = perl;
  - INPUT switched after the first line, and back after the second: each line decoded by the format in force, EOF and position 11 right (the position save / restore is REQUIRED: without it the read-ahead is lost -- "end of file");
  - a READ-WRITE file stream and a PIPE (switched before the first read): right;
  - 200,000 switches: buffer-p T on an input stream LEAKS (RSS 29 -> 84 MB); buffer-p NIL does not grow and reads correctly -- so NIL.
SO THE FIX: %p-rebuild-fd-stream stops dup-ing, building and closing; it re-installs in place and returns the SAME stream.  Everything keyed on the stream object (0, the fork-pipe pid, 0) then needs no carrying, and `%p-install-fh` is not called at all, so no variable is rewritten.  The standard handles keep their own path (%p-std-rebuild).
WHAT THE BATCH MUST SETTLE: (1) the routine is INTERNAL and its argument list is version-specific (8 arguments on 2.6.0: stream, element-type, canonized format, entry, input-p, output-p, buffer-p, dual-channel-p; older SBCLs took 6) -- decide at load time from `sb-introspect:function-lambda-list` (or a guarded trial call on a scratch stream); on a shape it does not know, keep TODAY's rebuild and say so once on stderr under PCL_FASL_DEBUG-style diagnostics, never silently pick an argument order; the supported floor is SBCL 2.5.2 (CLAUDE.md) -- say what it has; (2) dual-channel-p: NIL was right for files and a pipe; probe a SOCKET and a tty; (3) a partly-read NON-seekable input (pipe / socket / tty) cannot be re-sought: the characters already decoded stay decoded the old way -- perl has the same caveat, say what PCL does; (4) the probe table of this task (every way a handle gets a second name x binmode to and from :raw / :utf8 / :encoding(UTF-8) / :crlf, output and partly-read input) against perl; (5) `open(my $dup, ">&", $fh)` is a REAL second descriptor and must stay independent; (6) a platform-touching change: the install matrix and a macOS leg green before it ships (USER 2026-09-06).
GUARD ROWS: b1.pl .. b5.pl and u.pl of ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s510/review/binmode/ (perl: 6 / 0-in-process / 4 / 6 / 11 bytes).

=== DONE (s510b, Opus 5.5; commit 261da5bb on the s510b branch, rebased s512) ===
binmode re-formats the stream IN PLACE: %p-rebuild-fd-stream re-installs the SAME fd-stream's routines through SBCL's internal set-fd-stream-routines (buffer-p NIL, input position saved and re-sought, dual-channel-p from synchronize-output); no dup / close / %p-install-fh, so every name for the handle (copy, sub argument, hash/array slot, closure, object, IO ref, local glob) keeps writing to the one stream.  The internal routine is admitted by its LAMBDA LIST, decided once at load (identical on SBCL 2.5.2 and 2.6.0); any other shape keeps the old dup-and-rebuild (%p-rebuild-fd-stream-by-dup), announced under PCL_FASL_DEBUG.  Socket pair and /dev/tty probed = perl; leak bounded (200k and 800k switches both 74 MB RSS); open($dup, '>&', $fh) stays independent.  ir-spec 7.7.  Guard Pl/t/binmode-01.t 6 -> 13 rows (b1..b5, u.pl), inverse-verified on 3ea47a41.  Handle-names table: base 5/20 per name, tree 11/20 = globref (every name agrees).
RESIDUE: an in-memory handle carries CHARACTERS, so binmode($mem, ':utf8') + print "\x{e9}" leaves 1 char where perl leaves 2 bytes -- pre-existing, documented in %p-binmode-impl (review r.pl row 10).  Filed: #2851 (binmode "" pops to bytes), #2852 (partly-read PIPE loses read-ahead; not-supported), #2853 (explicit :crlf is not a no-op on Unix; not-supported bullet corrected).  macOS leg NOT run (CI has no macOS job).
subject: SILENT DATA LOSS (pre-existing, everyday file I/O): `binmode($h, ":utf8")` through a COPY of a lexical filehandle (a helper sub\x27s `my ($h) = @_`, or `my $g = $fh`) leaves every OTHER name for the handle on a CLOSED stream -- the caller\x27s later `print $fh` writes nothing and its `close` flushes nothing
